Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables cell-type-specific prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in the kidney, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and conditions. This approach provides a practical alternative to training new models de novo.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes involved in 'floatptosis,' a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data, the authors link floatptosis-related gene expression to patient survival and immunotherapy response. The work is exploratory and the clinical utility of the model remains to be validated.

Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.

The authors built a senescence-associated prognostic model for bladder urothelial carcinoma by screening pan-cancer senescence signals and integrating multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signatures to tumor microenvironment features, aiming to connect molecular characterization with clinical translation.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a new Python package that simplifies the design of DNA sequence libraries for high-throughput experiments like MPRAs, deep mutational scanning, and MAVEs. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software, reducing errors and tedium in library design, and can also be used to generate sequences for testing genomic AI models.

Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.

This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Using existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive power of these epigenetic marks for fertility outcomes. The work represents an initial step toward developing an operational tool for fertility prediction in dairy cattle.

Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.

The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab, a free community-supported web platform that packages over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of microbial omics data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers so microbiologists without bioinformatics expertise can run metabarcoding, metagenomic, and metatranscriptomic analyses.

Verix: a toolkit for benchmarking and harmonization of complex structural variants.

Verix is a new software toolkit that benchmarks and harmonizes complex structural variants (CSVs), which are large genomic rearrangements involving multiple breakpoints. Existing evaluation frameworks only handle simple single-breakpoint variants, so Verix fills a gap by quantifying how accurately multi-breakpoint CSV events are reconstructed and by distinguishing different types of reconstruction errors. This enables more systematic development and comparison of CSV detection methods.

MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.

MitImpact 4 expands a mitochondrial variant database to cover all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants across the entire mitochondrial genome, including tRNA and rRNA genes that were previously neglected. It provides functional annotations for both coding and non-coding variants, addressing a diagnostic blind spot for pathogenic mitochondrial alleles whose effects depend on RNA structure rather than protein sequence.

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs in three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs under FDR control, including 9 shared across cell lines. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. This provides an experimental benchmark for evaluating computational regulatory variant predictions.

Ultra-sensitive Mapping of Cell-free DNA-derived Methylomes Reveals Brain-specific Epigenetic Alterations Implicated in Alzheimer's Disease.

The authors applied LABS, an ultra-sensitive linear amplification-based whole-genome bisulfite sequencing method, to profile methylation in serum cell-free DNA from age- and sex-matched participants with pathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease versus non-AD controls. They detected brain-derived epigenetic alterations in the blood cfDNA methylome that distinguish AD cases, suggesting cfDNA methylation could serve as a minimally invasive biomarker for AD.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the full workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The paper introduces Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model coverage variation across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across diverse tissues and disease states. This approach reveals disease-relevant RNA processing changes that are missed by annotation-dependent methods.

Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.

Viscous mechanical cues encode metastatic behavior through cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling.

This study shows that the viscosity of a tumor's mechanical environment can mimic the effects of stiffness on cancer cells. Cells grown on soft but viscous substrates adopt stiffness-like behaviors, including increased cell stiffness, nuclear YAP accumulation, and enhanced migration through narrow constrictions, with accompanying epigenomic and transcriptomic changes. The work suggests viscous cues are decoded through cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling to drive metastatic behavior.

Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.

This paper argues that widely used computational variant effect predictors are biased by ancestry because their training data under-represent global populations, leading to unequal classification accuracy across ancestries. The authors propose combining multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) with population-free computational predictors to produce ancestry-agnostic evidence for classifying variants in hereditary cancer genes. This combined approach aims to improve fairness and generalizability of variant classification across diverse populations.

Bivalent Inhibitor Development for a Dynamic Epigenetic Tandem Reader Protein Using a Combinatorial Histone Code.

This preprint describes the development of bivalent inhibitors targeting BPTF, an epigenetic reader protein that contains a PHD finger and tandem bromodomains. The authors use a combinatorial histone code approach to design chemical probes that engage multiple reader domains simultaneously, aiming to improve selectivity and potency for this dynamic epigenetic target. The work provides a structural and chemical framework for targeting tandem reader proteins implicated in disease and cancer.

Same-cell mapping of epigenetic regulatory state to functional proteomic output.

The authors introduce Proteo-Seq, a single-cell method that simultaneously profiles chromatin accessibility and cytoplasmic protein output from the same cell. The device uses a two-layer microwell stack with a dissolvable gel trapdoor to route cytoplasmic proteins to targeted or discovery proteomics while transferring intact nuclei to snATAC-seq. This enables direct mapping of epigenetic regulatory state to functional proteomic output at single-cell resolution.

Nanopore Sequencing for Epigenetic Decoding: Applications, Analytical Constraints, and Translational Prospects.

This review examines how nanopore sequencing can decode multiple epigenetic layers—DNA and RNA modifications, histone marks, and chromatin accessibility—from long reads, potentially integrating information that is usually gathered in separate assays. It discusses analytical constraints and translational prospects for using nanopore-based epigenetics in research and clinical settings.

A step forward in comprehensive nanopore-based forensic profiling of STRs, InDel, SNP and mtDNA for identity and appearance prediction.

This study demonstrates that Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing can simultaneously profile multiple forensic DNA markers—STRs, InDels, SNPs, mtDNA variants, and DNA methylation—in a single assay. Translational oncology 2026-Oct-16 Medium

Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.

This review examines whether cell-free DNA fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5hmC profiling add complementary information beyond mutation-based liquid biopsy in hematologic malignancies, where clonal hematopoiesis and treatment-related changes complicate variant interpretation. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, but most studies remain retrospective with only internal validation. The authors highlight translational limitations and outline future directions for clinical implementation.

Single-cell variant landscape of the human mitochondrial genome reveals cell type-specific functions and disease mechanisms.

The authors present scMOCHA, a scalable computational framework that infers high-confidence single-cell mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy directly from standard scRNA-seq data. Applying it to public human PBMC datasets, they reveal cell type-specific patterns of mtDNA variants and link them to cellular functions and disease mechanisms. This work establishes single-cell mtDNA heteroplasmy as a tractable dimension of cellular genetic diversity.

Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.
